questions.instruction: Examine the sender address. Is this email legitimate?
questions.teaching_point: Always check the actual sender domain — not just the display name.

headers.subject: Your account has been temporarily locked

clues.label: Spoofed domain
clues.explanation: Real ING emails come from @ing.nl. 'ing-secure-alerts.com' is a lookalike registered by attackers.

clues.label: Suspicious Reply-To
clues.explanation: Replies route to a .ru domain — completely unrelated to ING.

emails.explanation: Classic bank impersonation. The domain and Reply-To mismatch both confirm phishing.

headers.subject: [GitHub] A new SSH key was added to your account

clues.label: No Reply-To trick
clues.explanation: No separate Reply-To — replies stay on github.com.

emails.explanation: Legitimate GitHub security notification. Domain verified, no mismatch.

questions.instruction: Read the email body. Hover over links to see where they actually go.
questions.teaching_point: Hover over links before clicking — the real URL often reveals the truth. HTTP links on login pages are always suspicious.

clues.label: Lookalike domain
clues.explanation: Real DigiD is @digid.nl. 'digid-verificatie.com' is a fake.

clues.label: HTTP link
clues.explanation: No legitimate government service uses HTTP for login pages.

clues.label: 12-hour threat
clues.explanation: Government agencies never delete accounts by email within hours.

emails.explanation: DigiD phishing — one of the most common in the Netherlands. Domain, HTTP link and urgency all confirm it.

headers.subject: You appeared in 12 searches this week

body.content: Your profile is getting attention — 12 searches this week.

clues.label: Real domain
clues.explanation: messages-noreply@linkedin.com is a verified LinkedIn domain.

clues.label: HTTPS links
clues.explanation: Both links resolve to www.linkedin.com over HTTPS.

emails.explanation: Legitimate LinkedIn notification. Domain, HTTPS links, and no credential request all check out.

questions.instruction: Analyse everything — headers and body. Some emails look very polished.
questions.teaching_point: Spear phishing uses your real name and company details. The only reliable indicator is often the sender domain.

body.content: Your account has reached 92% storage. Act within 48 hours.
ICT Helpdesk — Radboud University, Houtlaan 4, Nijmegen

clues.label: Lookalike domain
clues.explanation: Radboud's real domain is ru.nl. 'ru-ict-support.nl' is a separately registered fake.

clues.label: Spear phishing
clues.explanation: Uses your real name and university address — harvested from public sources.

clues.label: 48-hour pressure
clues.explanation: ICT departments send warnings well in advance. Urgent email links are not a helpdesk workflow.

emails.explanation: Sophisticated spear phishing. Uses real name and address — but the domain is ru-ict-support.nl, not ru.nl.

body.content: Reminder: thesis submission deadline is 28 March 2025 at 23:59.

clues.label: Real ru.nl domain
clues.explanation: noreply@ru.nl is Radboud's verified sending domain.

clues.label: HTTPS portal link
clues.explanation: Button resolves to https://www.ru.nl — same domain as sender.

clues.label: No urgency tricks
clues.explanation: Calm, specific, with a real contact address.

emails.explanation: Legitimate Radboud notification. Domain, HTTPS link, and calm tone confirm it.
